text:
Carlos: Quick idea — expose a small client-visible header with a coarse queue/wait estimate so callers can choose retry vs degrade. e.g. "X-Redwood-Queue". Thoughts?

Tanvi: +1 on visibility. Couple concerns: do we leak tenant load fingerprints? might be useful for attackers to probe.

Carlos: Good call. My thought is to keep it coarse buckets instead of exact ms, and include an optional opaque token for traceability. Example header:
```
X-Redwood-Queue: bucket=2; est=70ms; token=rz4kQ
```
Buckets: 0=(<50ms),1=(50-200ms),2=(200-500ms),3=(>500ms)

Pranav: Where do you compute that? edge proxy or admission service? Edge gives freshest numbers but the admission service already has the fairness state.

Carlos: I was leaning admission service because it knows queue/lease decisions. Edge could add small added latency if it has to call admission. Tradeoff.

Liz: Ops note — if we expose this header to unauthenticated clients it becomes a reconnaissance channel. Two mitigations: only for authenticated API keys, or return coarse buckets and rate-limit repeated header reads.

Carlos: Agreed. Also thought about signing or HMAC-ing the token so clients can’t fabricate. But signing every response might be heavy.

Pranav: Alternative: token is just an opaque id referencing a short-lived admission record in our cache (redis). Clients get the opaque token; only internal debug endpoints can resolve it. So no HMAC needed, and minimal header size.

Tanvi: I like opaque token approach. Also recommend a feature flag: expose_header=[false|coarse|detailed] per tenant. Default coarse for safety.

Liz: We should also ensure the header can't be used to inflate priority (e.g., avoid clients resubmitting until bucket drops). Add server-side anti-probing: throttle header-return frequency per key.

Carlos: Config knobs I'd propose in RFC: buckets, token-ttl, expose_for_unauth (bool), header-rate-limit, store-in-admission-or-edge enum. I'll sketch perf/cost implications.

Pranav: Implementation notes: admission service computes bucket & may emit token to redis with value {tenant, bucket, created_at, reason}. Edge can optionally ask admission service with a cheap lookup to attach header. That keeps admission authoritative.

Tanvi: Also add telemetry: histogram of reported buckets vs actual enqueue time to detect drift and gaming.

Liz: And admin tools: allow resolving tokens (admin-only) and an alert if tokens resolved frequently from same external IP (probing).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout window scheduled next Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC for admission-service. See https://deploys.redwood.internal/1234 :rocket:

Carlos: OK I'll file a follow-up RFC with the config shape and sample header semantics, assign prototype to Tanvi + me. Pranav can own cache layer.

Pranav: assigning: Pranav -> cache infra; Carlos -> RFC + admission changes; Tanvi -> prototype + telemetry sketch.

Tanvi: :raised_hands: will draft perf numbers and a brief attack-surface section.
